h1: Band saw blades for metal cutting — bimetal M42 and carbide-tipped
intro: A band saw blade is the one consumable that decides what a band saw machine can do: the right cutting material, tooth form and tooth pitch cut faster, straighter and longer than the wrong one on any saw. NovoTech supplies the two WIKUS blades that Canadian shops run most — made in Germany by the world's largest band saw blade maker and welded to the length of your machine in Mississauga, ON. The MARATHON® M42 bimetal blade is the everyday blade for profiles, tube, bundles and solid bar on any horizontal or vertical band saw; the FUTURA® carbide-tipped blade is the production blade for solid steel, stainless and aluminum on the Bekamak saws and any machine with a carbide package. Both come in every width from 1/2″ to 3-1/8″ and in every tooth pitch; the rest of the WIKUS program — coated PREMIUM blades, X3000® blades for difficult alloys, the NE blades for aluminum and copper, CBN-coated blades for hardened steel — is available to order.

groups.title: Bimetal band saw blade — MARATHON® M42
groups.lead: The universal bimetal blade: an M42 high-speed-steel cutting edge welded to a spring-steel back, for profiles, tube, bundles and solid material to 1,000 N/mm² (145,000 psi) on any horizontal or vertical band saw. The blade most Canadian fabrication shops run every day — and the one NovoTech stocks as coil.

groups.title: Carbide-tipped band saw blade — FUTURA®
groups.lead: The universal carbide-tipped blade for production sawing of solid material: ground carbide teeth on an alloyed spring-steel back, two to three times the cutting rate of a bimetal blade and far longer blade life on the Bekamak production saws and any saw with a carbide package.

faq.q: Bimetal or carbide — which band saw blade do I need?
faq.a: The MARATHON M42 bimetal blade (M42 high-speed-steel teeth on a spring-steel back) is the right blade for a fabrication shop: structural profiles, tube, bundles and solid bar up to about 145,000 psi, mixed materials, on any band saw. The FUTURA carbide-tipped blade cuts solid material two to three times faster and lasts several times longer, but it wants a rigid saw with enough motor power and band tension — the Bekamak production saws and most saws with a carbide package. If most of your cutting is solid bar, plate strips or stainless on such a saw, the FUTURA pays for itself; for everything else, the MARATHON.

faq.q: How do I choose the tooth pitch?
faq.a: By the contact length — the width of material the blade is in at any moment: 4 to 12 teeth should be in the cut. Thin-wall tube and small profiles need a fine pitch (10–14 TPI), bar of 2 to 4 inches a 3–4 or 2–3 TPI blade, and large solid material 1.4–2 TPI and coarser. A variable pitch (for example 3–4 TPI) runs quieter and resists vibration on profiles and bundles; a constant pitch is used on uniform solid material. Each blade's table on this page lists the pitches available in every width and the contact length each pitch is meant for.

faq.q: Which blade width and length fits my saw?
faq.a: The width and thickness are set by the saw's wheels and guides — 1″ × 0.035″ on most 10″ to 13″ shop saws, 1-1/4″ × 0.042″ and 1-1/2″ × 0.050″ on the mid-size automatic saws, 2″ to 3-1/8″ on the double-column production saws. The length is the loop length of your machine; we weld the blade to it from coil. Send the saw make and model and we look it up.

faq.q: Can the FUTURA carbide blade run on my saw?
faq.a: On the Bekamak BMSO and BMSY automatic saws, the double-column saws and any saw with a carbide package (high band tension, rigid guides, enough motor power) — yes. On a lighter saw, stay with the MARATHON M42, or ask us about the TAURUS, a carbide blade set and ground to run without the carbide package.

faq.q: Do you supply other WIKUS blades?
faq.a: Yes — the complete WIKUS metal-cutting program is available to order: the economical PRIMAR and the high-performance SKALAR and SELEKTA GS bimetal blades, the coated PREMIUM versions, the X3000® blades for stainless, nickel and titanium alloys, the DUROSET and TAURUS carbide blades, the FUTURA VA, 718, NE and SN specialists for stainless, superalloys, aluminum and hardened parts, and the CUBOGRIT® CBN blades for hardened steel above 55 HRC. Tell us the material and the saw and we propose the blade; data sheets on request.

faq.q: Do you stock blades and weld them in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — the common widths of the MARATHON M42 are stocked as coil in Mississauga and welded and annealed to your length; the FUTURA and the rest of the program are welded to order. Tell us the saw, the materials you cut and the sizes, and we propose the blade and the pitch — and we are happy to run a test blade on a difficult job.

origin_feature.title: Made in Germany by WIKUS
origin_feature.text: WIKUS has made band saw blades in Spangenberg, Germany since 1958 — bimetal, carbide-tipped and coated blades for metal cutting, developed in its own Technical Competence Center and cut and welded to length by its partners worldwide.
